_comment: Where every tool comes from and how to recognise it.
NOTHING HERE IS VENDORED. This file describes tools that live at
'root' below; it never contains one. 'detect' is how we know a tool is
really present and which version -- probing rather than trusting a path
is what stops a half-finished install from looking like a working one.
'install' is deliberately a URL plus a human instruction, not an
automated silent installer. Several of these vendors require accepting a
licence or registering, and scripting around that would be both fragile
Globs are version-agnostic on purpose: every one of these was first written as a fixed path and every one of them was wrong. A toolchain upgrade must not silently turn into 'missing'.

install.note: Installer adds itself to PATH. Free, GPL.

sdcc.note: Primary 8051 compiler. No C++ mode at all, which is why an 8051 Arduino core needs IAR instead.

install.note: Commercial, size-limited evaluation available. Requires registration; cannot be scripted.

iar_8051.note: The only 8051 compiler here with C++ (--eec++), so the only one an Arduino core can be built on.

install.note: Free tier works; unoptimised but complete. Silent install supported.
Free. C++14 capable, which is why a C2000 Arduino core is possible.
Portable: unpack to C:/embd_toolchains/arm and add bin to PATH for the session.

arm_none_eabi.note: Carried here for the simulator even though Arduino cores exist -- a simulator needs a toolchain it controls.

install.note: Portable xPack build. Unpack to C:/embd_toolchains/riscv.

usbasp.note: SPI ISP. A crystal MUST be running on the target or ISP never responds -- the commonest failure by a wide margin.

nano_at89c2051.note: The AT89C2051 has NO ISP at all. It needs a 12 V parallel programming sequence, so we build the programmer ourselves on a Nano.

stcgal.note: Serial bootloader, entered by power-cycling the target while the tool waits. STC89 parts can ALSO be done over SPI ISP with a USB-ISP; STC15 cannot.

pickit3.note: Dropped by MPLAB X 6.x. Use MPLAB IPE 5.50 or earlier, or a PICkit 4/5.
